label: Kazakh Bactrian

links.name: Razuan et al. 2025, Brazilian Journal of Biology

names.text: The article calls the Kazakh Bactrian the 'Kazakh Bactrian (double-humped) camel'. The alias 'Kazakh camel' from the brief was not confirmed in any page opened, so it is left out.

about.text: The Kazakh Bactrian is a double-humped camel kept on farms across Kazakhstan, including the steppe zones of the West, Kyzylorda, South Kazakhstan, Mangystau and Western regions. In a 2021 to 2023 study of farms in the Turkestan region, its milk averaged 5.56 litres a day, and the article states that milk is the main product of the females.

links.name: Razuan et al. 2025, Brazilian Journal of Biology

sources.text: Farm study in the Turkestan region, 2021 to 2023, with Kazakh Bactrian and Turkmen dromedary camels. Regions listed from the article's population descriptions. Daily yield from Table 4 (n=30). Main-product statement paraphrased from the article's text.

links.name: Razuan et al. 2025, Brazilian Journal of Biology

sources.text: Place only: the article reports the breed on farms and in regions of Kazakhstan. It does not say where or when the breed was formed, so no formation years are given.

links.name: Razuan et al. 2025, Brazilian Journal of Biology

sources.text: The article says milk is the main product of female camels, and that the breed is also used for meat and wool. Dairy is listed first as the main product.

links.name: Razuan et al. 2025, Brazilian Journal of Biology

sources.text: Fat 5.5 to 7.0 percent for the Kazakh Bactrian, from the Results and Conclusions. No raw-milk protein figure for this breed is given in the article.

facts.v: 5.56 litres a day (±0.14) on average, against 7.60 litres for the Turkmen dromedary in the same farm study (n=30).

links.name: Razuan et al. 2025, Brazilian Journal of Biology

sources.text: Table 4 of the article, Kazakh Bactrian 5.56 ± 0.14 L and Turkmen dromedary 7.60 ± 0.15 L.

facts.v: About 2,879 litres over the milking season (2878.6 litres in the article).

links.name: Razuan et al. 2025, Brazilian Journal of Biology

sources.text: Milking-season total from the article's Conclusions, Kazakh Bactrian 2878.6 L. The article does not give the season's length in days.

facts.v: Under three-times-daily milking, daily yield peaked at 8.89 litres in August and ranged from 4.95 to 8.89 litres.

links.name: Razuan et al. 2025, Brazilian Journal of Biology

sources.text: Results section of the article, Kazakh Bactrian under three-times-daily milking.

gaps: Searched for and could not find: the breed's origin and formation dates (not in the article); a breed-specific population count (the article gives only national totals, 282.8 thousand camels in Kazakhstan on 1 January 2024); a DAD-IS record and risk status (a DAD-IS URL returned 404 and a search found no DAD-IS page for this breed); protein percentage and lactation length for this breed; the alias 'Kazakh camel'. Yield per lactation is left out because the article reports a milking season, not a lactation. The 'why' line says the breed is the one Bactrian population classed as dairy in the sources opened; that comparison was not checked against other breeds beyond the one article.
